_comment: Hand-verified citation facts for Module 11 (Safety breaches). Each entry was confirmed by reading the reconstructed decision text from fwc-decision-chunks.snapshot.db -- never from decision_extracts model fields. download_id, jurisdiction and decision_date are cross-checked against briefer_master.snapshot.db by build_citation_registry.py.

[2024] FWC 2154.outcome: Dismissal of a cabin crew member for an alcohol-policy breach found not to give rise to a valid reason in the circumstances; dismissal found unfair. The Commission separately found that even if the breach had been a valid reason, dismissal would still have been harsh.

[2025] FWC 2551.outcome: A valid reason was found for dismissing an experienced scaffolder who deliberately ignored a scaffold safety rule, even though no one was actually injured. The dismissal was nonetheless found unfair because of a rushed, procedurally unfair process, and the Commission ordered 2 weeks' pay plus superannuation rather than reinstatement or a larger compensation award.

[2025] FWC 2819.short_name: Khouri v Coulson Aviation (Australia) Pty Ltd
[2025] FWC 2819.outcome: No valid reason found for dismissing a helicopter pilot following a serious in-flight incident investigated under the employer's Safety Management System. The Commission found the pilot had engaged honestly and constructively with the safety investigation, and that disciplining him for alleged airmanship failures was inconsistent with the employer's own 'Just Culture' principles. Dismissal found harsh, unjust and unreasonable; reinstatement with continuity of service and back pay ordered.

[2020] FWC 3919.short_name: Pavlovic v Alcoa of Australia Limited
[2020] FWC 3919.outcome: Dismissal of a mineworker for failing to isolate fixed plant equipment before maintenance -- a near-miss with no actual injury but a real risk of death or serious injury -- found not unfair. The Commission rejected an inconsistency argument based on a comparator who caused an actual electrocution and hospitalisation but received only a final warning, and a second comparator involved in the same incident, on the basis that the underlying culpability differed in each case.
